set.pl: Port Sheldon townsite at the outlet of Pigeon Lake (1876 atlas: the only building cluster, S shore NW sec 21 T6N R16W); which shore held the Ottawa House is unconfirmed; the power plant now covers the N side
set.st: An 1874 letter from Gorton L. Scott, left in charge of the Ottawa House after the Port Sheldon land bubble burst, says two strangers who stopped there one October night were murdered by 'Irish Mike' and Dennis, and their bodies and 'some of the plunder' were buried 'near the run at the base of the blow-hole, just west of the hotel'. Scott searched about 1871, but 'shifting sands' had changed the bluffs. Pin is the townsite at the lake outlet, not the spot.
pinev: 1876 Ottawa-Kent atlas, Olive Twp (T6N R16W): Pigeon Lake straddles secs 15/16 and 21/22; the only buildings are a small cluster (one starred) at the outlet, S shore, NW sec 21; the head of the lake (sec 15) has none and no hotel is labelled. The 1874 letter's 'blow-hole just west of the hotel' fits the Lake Michigan dune ridge at the outlet, not the head.
Meima's map reading (head of lake) now set aside; lidar read of the outlet dunes queued.
Pin on land about 250 m S of the Pigeon Lake shore (ArcGIS detailed water outline), r400.

src: Illustrated Historical Atlas of the Counties of Ottawa and Kent, Michigan (1876), Olive Twp T6N R16W (archive.org 3927947, leaf 32)

pinev: GNIS Port Sheldon, on land S of Pigeon Lake (2016 Michigan 1 m lidar). On the lidar the power plant and its round pond lie N of the lake, so the 400 m ring stays on the S (townsite) side; no street grid or maple avenue shows.

The Ottawa House (two storeys, 80 x 150 ft) stood 'not far from the head of Pigeon Lake', on the NE shore per the old company map (Meima 1921, No. III). On 2016 lidar the lake runs about 3 km E of the pin to its head near -86.162, so that shore is far outside the ring; the hotel was only where the company lived, not the cache spot, so the pin stays on the townsite.
1912 Ottawa plat, Olive Twp: the NE head of Pigeon Lake (secs 15-16) is Gooding/Olman land at the Pigeon River mouth; no hotel shown

1876 Ottawa-Kent atlas, Olive Twp: the only building cluster on Pigeon Lake (one starred) is at the outlet, S shore NW sec 21 T6N R16W, about 700 m W of this pin; the head of the lake (sec 15) has none and no hotel is labelled.

src: Illustrated Historical Atlas of the Counties of Ottawa and Kent, Michigan (1876), Olive Twp T6N R16W (archive.org 3927947, leaf 32)
